item.title: Global Energy Import Dependence Set to Peak by 2034, Rystad Says
item.description: Rystad Energy’s fifth edition of its flagship annual report, Global Energy Scenarios (GES) 2026, finds that global reliance on imported energy is projected to peak by 2034 as energy security concerns accelerate the shift towards electrification. Against the backdrop of two major energy crises in five years, the report highlights how a broader range of rapidly deployable technologies is helping the energy system withstand major disruptions to energy flows. item.title: Norway's Untapped Oil and Gas Frontier Is Drawing Renewed Interest
item.description: More than three decades after Norway opened parts of the Norwegian Sea to petroleum exploration, potentially significant oil and gas resources remain hidden beneath thick layers of volcanic rock. Now, advances in exploration technology and renewed industry interest could bring one of Europe's least explored offshore frontiers back into focus. Norway may still hold substantial undiscovered oil and gas resources in areas that have remained virtually untouched by exploration drilling for more than 30 years. item.title: U.S. Offers Another 17 Million SPR Barrels as Fuel Crisis Deepens
item.description: The United States is putting another 17 million barrels of crude from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve on offer, one day after the IEA accelerated emergency stock releases as governments scramble to get more oil and fuel into a tight market. The Department of Energy issued a request for proposals Friday for an exchange of up to 17 million barrels, part of the 172 million barrels Washington committed to make available under the IEA’s 400-million-barrel emergency action announced in March. item.description: A massive wind farm in the state of Victoria, Australia, has been approved by state authorities, paving the way for the project to go to the federal environment minister for final checks. ABC News reports Planning Minister Sonya Kilkenny this week signed off on the Warracknabeal Energy Park, five months after its environmental impact report was approved. item.title: U.S. Oil Drillers Back Off Even As Prices Soar
item.description: The total number of active drilling rigs for oil and gas in the United States remained unchanged this week, according to new data that Baker Hughes published on Friday, with the total rig count in the US staying at 603, up 55 from this same time last year. The number of active oil rigs fell by 3, to 459 during the latest reporting period, according to the data. This is 41 above this same time last year. item.title: Equatorial Guinea Rewrites Oil Law After Production Collapses 85%
item.description: Equatorial Guinea will approve a new hydrocarbon law on Monday after crude production collapsed to just 20,000 barrels per day in September, down from roughly 140,000 bpd in 2020. The 120,000-bpd loss has reduced OPEC’s smallest producer to a fraction of its former output and contributed to an economy the International Monetary Fund expects to shrink 1.7% this year. item.title: Oil Prices Are Stuck at $105 as Geopolitical Risks Mount
item.description: Brent holds near $105 as Iranian tanker attacks and multiple geopolitical conflicts keep oil markets on edge. item.title: IMF Sounds Alarm Over AI’s Threat to Government Tax Bases
item.description: The head of the International Monetary Fund has warned financial ministers that widespread AI adoption could erode tax bases across the world as incomes are squeezed by the technology. Kristalina Georgieva, the managing director of the IMF, said governments may be ill-prepared for a potential slump in tax revenue brought on by AI’s impact on the labour market. item.description: Two startup electricity retailers in Germany have recently announced they would cease operations as spiking wholesale prices amid the gas price surge are pressuring the industry again, and this time the pressure is compounded by plans for renewable policy changes. item.title: Global Gas Crunch Makes Europe’s Remaining Coal Plants Profitable
item.description: The global LNG supply crunch has made Europe’s last-standing coal-fired power plants profitable this year as gas supply costs soar while the need for conventional generation to stabilize grids remains. item.title: Iran War Set To Push PetroChina’s Trading Profit to Record $3 Billion
item.description: The trading arm of China’s state-owned giant PetroChina is set to reap a record more than $3 billion (20 billion yuan) in trading profits this year as the Middle East crisis hiked crude prices and rattled global fuel markets and trade flows.
